## Summary

Benzil undergoes the benzilic acid rearrangement in aqueous ethanolic potassium hydroxide. This is sample data; the quantities are not experimentally verified.

## Reagents

| Reagent | CAS | MW (g/mol) | Amount | mmol | Equiv |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Benzil | 134-81-6 | 210.23 | 2.102 g | 10 | 1.0 |
| Potassium hydroxide | 1310-58-3 | 56.11 | 1.122 g | 20 | 2.0 |
| Ethanol | 64-17-5 | 46.07 | 15 mL | – | – |
| Hydrogen chloride | 7647-01-0 | 36.46 | 2 M, 15 mL | – | – |

## Procedure

1. Dissolve potassium hydroxide in 3 mL water.
2. Place benzil and ethanol in a flask and add the base solution.
3. Fit a reflux condenser and stir the mixture.
4. Heat at reflux for 45 minutes.
5. Cool to room temperature and add 20 mL water.
6. Add 2 M hydrochloric acid slowly until acidic to indicator paper, then cool in ice.

## Workup and Purification

Collect the precipitate by suction filtration, wash with cold water and dry. Expected yield: 1.60 g (7.00 mmol, 70 %).

## Characterization

White crystals; expected IR bands near 3400 (O–H) and 1700 cm⁻¹ (carboxylic acid C=O).

## Notes

1. Add the acid slowly to control warming.
2. Check acidity after thorough mixing.
3. Cooling promotes crystallisation of the acid.

## Hazards and Waste Disposal

Benzil: may irritate skin and eyes; Potassium hydroxide: corrosive; causes severe burns; Ethanol: highly flammable; eye irritant; Hydrogen chloride: acidic solution irritates or burns skin and eyes; Benzilic acid: may irritate skin and eyes. Work in a fume hood; wear gloves and eye protection. Collect acidic aqueous filtrates and ethanol-containing liquids in the appropriate labelled waste containers.

## References

1. Furniss, B. S.; Hannaford, A. J.; Smith, P. W. G.; Tatchell, A. R. Vogel's Textbook of Practical Organic Chemistry, 5th ed.; Longman: Harlow, 1989.
